question: In the fortnight before a big race, what should an athlete cut to taper well: training volume or intensity?
answer: Volume. Pooling taper studies, Bosquet and colleagues found the best results came from tapers of about two weeks that cut weekly training volume by roughly 41 to 60%, while keeping intensity and the number of sessions the same. Easy, gentle weeks lose the sharpness that hard sessions keep: fewer kilometres, still run at speed.
move: To rest without going stale, cut the amount and keep the edge.
source: Bosquet et al., Med Sci Sports Exerc, 2007
reference: Bosquet, Montpetit, Arvisais & Mujika, Effects of tapering on performance: a meta-analysis, Medicine & Science in Sports & Exercise, 2007
